# Mules Grassfield

Mules Grassfield is the *Pulp Fiction* lookalike in a Manehattan diner: a background Earth-pony stallion modeled on Samuel L. Jackson’s Jules Winnfield, seated alongside a pony resembling Vincent Vega. Despite “Mules” in his name, he is a pony, not a mule.

- **Appearance:** Dusty-rose/mauve coat, dark plum curly mane, gray-green eyes, and a suitcase cutie mark. His dark suit and distinctive hairstyle make the movie reference recognizable.
- **Name:** “Mules Grassfield” is a community-used pony pun on *Jules Winnfield*. I found no verified on-screen introduction, production credit, or licensed naming source establishing it as an official character name; the original coiner is unconfirmed. The character *appears in the official G4 television continuity*, regardless of the name’s status. The [season-six allusions reference](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/List_of_allusions/Season_six) identifies the diner pair as allusions to Jules and Vincent.
- **Speaking:** No identified dialogue or confirmed voice actor.
- **Appearances:** *The Saddle Row Review* (season 6, episode 9; May 21, 2016) is his documented appearance. The later movie character **Whinnyfield** is a *separate* Jules-inspired pony, not an established alias, transformation, or return of Mules Grassfield; see the [movie-character listing](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/List_of_ponies/Unicorn_ponies).

## Important moments

- **The diner movie homage — “The Saddle Row Review” (S6E9).** In an early Manehattan diner scene, Mules Grassfield sits beside the Vincent Vega-inspired stallion, creating a brief visual joke rather than advancing the plot. [Official full episode](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sXZgcTz0ces) — **scene timestamp unavailable** (not independently verified against this upload).

Only one brief appearance is documented; there are no verified additional character-defining scenes to list.
